title: Alleged victim speaks out after former Coffee Co. deputy accused of tracking her is released on bond

reading.body:
This is a case of a system used outside the conditions it was built for. A law enforcement licence plate reader network and a state criminal database were built for police work, and the allegation is that a deputy queried them to track a woman for personal reasons. The failure sits at the access layer rather than in any model: the tools performed as designed, and the misuse was in who was asking and why.

Catching this kind of misuse requires logging that ties each query to a case or a stated purpose, and review that notices queries with no such justification. The reporting does not establish what audit or oversight was in place at the Coffee County sheriff's office, or whether any alert fired at the time.

The indictment is an allegation, and the eight counts are charges, not findings. Nothing in the reporting establishes guilt, and the outcome of the arraignment is not yet known.

reports.title: Alleged victim speaks out after former Coffee Co. deputy accused of tracking her is released on bond

summary:
A former Coffee County sheriff’s deputy, Chris Ashley Rozar, 49, was released on bond after a grand jury indicted him on eight counts, including four counts of violation of oath by a public officer, two counts of computer invasion of privacy, one count of prohibited use of captured license plate data, and one count of stalking. Investigators say he misused the sheriff’s office Flock camera and tag reader system and the GCIC database for personal reasons between April and May 2024, including tracking a woman without her consent.

The woman, who spoke anonymously, said she waited two years for the investigation and hopes her story encourages other women to report abuse. Rozar was arrested May 5 and released on bond the same day. He is scheduled for arraignment on May 27 in Coffee County Superior Court.
